articleTitle: A High-speed Low-cost CNN Inference Accelerator for Depthwise Separable Convolution
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-speed low-cost VLSI inference accelerator for depthwise separable convolution in deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The accelerator consists of parallel, pipelined depthwise convolution processing element array and pointwise convolution processing element array to improve system performance, with optimized hardware resource consumptions. Moreover, the PPE array can support fully-connected layers in CNNs. An FPGA prototype of the proposed accelerator was implemented. It executed a 12-layer simplified MobileNet model at a high speed above 15,000 frames per second (FPS) on $32\times 32$ images and 240 FPS on $224\times 224$ images.

articleTitle: High-PSR and fast-transient LDO regulator with nested adaptive FVF structure
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a low-dropout (LDO) regulator using nested adaptive flipped voltage follower (FVF) to achieve fast-transient response and improve both power supply rejection ratio (PSR) and line regulation. It features a maximum ripple of 4.6mV at output when the load current steps between 1μA and 20mA in 10ps, with the advantages of simulated PSR of -58.52dB at 1MHz and -41.66dB at 10MHz.

articleTitle: Real Time ECG Classification System Based on DWT and SVM
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) signal reflects the state of the heart. Arrhythmia detection in the ECG record plays a critical role in the clinical diagnosis of heart diseases. With the development of artificial intelligence technology in recent years, machine learning algorithms represented by Support Vector Machine (SVM) have been used for the classification of ECG signal. Based on the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and SVM classification algorithm, this work implements a hardware system including ECG signal acquisition, feature extraction and the classification on the Xilinx ZYNQ SoC. Especially, a power efficient DWT acceleration module is proposed. The system classification accuracy is 98.7% and the classification time of each heartbeat is 280 $\mu$ s with on-chip power of 2.059 W, which meets the requirement of real-time system.

articleTitle: Low Complexity ECG Biometric Authentication for IoT Edge Devices
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Wearable Internet of Things (IoT) devices are getting ubiquitous for continuous physiological data acquisition and health monitoring. This paper investigates an electrocardiogram (ECG) based biometric user authentication technique for IoT edge devices. A convolutional neural network (CNN) based deep learning technique for user authentication is proposed. The proposed technique achieves an authentication accuracy of 99.63% when tested with 290 subjects from Physionet PTB ECG database. To limit the complexity of the technique for IoT edge nodes, we applied optimisation techniques such as binarisation and approximation of the CNN weights. Accuracy-vs-time-complexity trade-off analysis is performed and results are presented for different optimisations. Our evaluations shows that the complexity-optimised method achieves 98.88% authentication accuracy with acceptable CPU cycles consumed.

articleTitle: Robot navigation based on pseudo-binocular stereo vision and linear fitting
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a pseudo-binocular stereo vision and linear fitting to achieve robot navigation. Pseudo-binocular stereo vision is realized by moving the robot body to the left or right with a certain distance. Then, a disparity map is calculated with the semi-global matching algorithm. This method can overcome the interference of complex color and texture for objects that are at the same distance. After edge detection and binarizing of the disparity map, road lines are extracted by the Hough transform algorithm. To extract the road lines from the noisy edges, the least square method for linear fitting is utilized for high-accuracy navigation.

articleTitle: The Optimization of Object Detection and Localization in Complex Background for Vision-based Robot
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper studies the object detection and localization for vision-based robots. The vision-based robot collects the stream of images by using the wide-angle monocular camera to get more-detailed information of objects around the robot. Based on the captured camera image, we first preprocess the collected image information to extract useful points by distortion correction, color space conversion and noise reduction. After getting color and shape information of object, we propose several algorithms to cancel the interfere from complex background with a close operation, to use a multi-threshold limitation for object detection and localization, and to find minimum circumscribed rectangle of target in order to recognize obstacles and adjust robot's direction and position. Finally, the robot performs well with the presented methods.

articleTitle: A circuit-algorithm codesign method to reduce the accuracy drop of RRAM based computing-in-memory chip
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Deep neural networks have exhibited superior performance in many areas such as image classification and so on. Due to the “memory bottleneck the energy efficiency of traditional chips is limited. The RRAM based computing-in-memory chip offers a new computing paradigm to remove data transfer between computing units and memory units. However, the nonidealities of RRAM device and analog circuits will reduce the on-chip accuracy. Here, we propose a novel codesign method to reduce the accuracy drop in the post-mapping phase of computing-in-memory system. First, we introduce the architecture of computing-in-memory chip and develop the compact model of the device and peripheral circuits. To reduce the accuracy drop, we present a novel codesign method by add nonidealities of device and circuits in the training phase of neural network. Finally, we found the post-mapping accuracy could recover more than 20% accuracy after device and circuit aware training.

articleTitle: Low-Voltage High-Linearity Differential Input Buffer with CurrentAmplifier Feed-Forward Compensation for High-Speed ADCs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A source-follower (SF) based differential input buffer for high speed ADCs, in which an auxiliary SF pair and a current amplifier pairs generate a differential compensation current injecting into the main SF pair to achieve linearization is presented. Designed in a 28nm CMOS, the two tone simulation (1.4-Vpp input at 5.92GHz and 5.98GHz) result with 6-GSPS sampling frequency, and 2.5-V VDD supply voltage shows that the buffer achieves an SFDR of 76.3dBFS, equivalent input noise about 200uV and offet 1mV at most while consumes only 150-mW power(Differential pair). Compared to the conventional structure, the proposed input buffer is more suitable for low-power and low-voltage applications, and brings smaller capacitive load to the input source.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of 5G N77 Bandpass Filter with HR-Si IPD Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A compact lumped high-selectivity bandpass filter suitable for 5G communication using high resistivity silicon integrated passive device (IPD) technology is presented in this paper. The use of IPD technology can effectively improve the integration of passive devices and reduce the size of devices, which is of great significance for the low-cost and miniaturized system design. The size of the designed bandpass filter is 2mm×1.25mm, and the passband frequency ranges from 3.3GHz to 4.2 GHz. The insertion loss is below 2.7dB over the pass band, and out-of-band attenuation exceeds 35dB from 0.45GHz to 2.4GHz as well as 36dB from 5.15GHz to 5.85GHz and 25.6dB from 6.6GHz to 8.4GHz. The design is verified through on-wafer measurement.

articleTitle: A Customized Low Static Leakage Near/Sub-threshold Standard Cell Library Using Thick-gate Transistors
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A full-customized standard cell library using thick-gate transistors in TSMC 65nm technology is proposed for low static power demand in long-term monitoring IoT systems. The transistors are working in near/sub-threshold region, and channel length are increased for drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL) effect inhibition. The standard cell layout area is optimized using dynamic N-well (NW) height. Algorithms are proposed for automatically DRC violations fixing due to cancellation of fillers. The customized standard cell library stands out for >400x smaller leakage power consumption compared to commercial library.

articleTitle: Accelerating Atrous Convolution with Fetch-and-Jump Architecture for Activation Positioning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Recent advancements in abundant applications of computer vision (CV) have attributed to convolutional neural network, which plays the primary role in feature extraction. For specific CV tasks such as semantic image segmentation, aggregation of multi-scale contextual information is demanded which leads to the adoption of atrous convolution. However, atrous convolution introduces extra performance overheads for conventional CPU and GPU machines, mainly due to inconstant latency of memory access caused by holes in atrous kernels. Such deterioration gets exaggerated especially during parallel processing of pixels in the output feature map. In this work, we first assemble continuous datastream by overlapping adjacent atrous kernels to avoid frequent update of memory access locations. By referring various patterns of atrous kernels, we introduce distributed fetch pointers to extract individual elements from assembled datastream while adaptively update pointer positions. A prototype dataflow accelerator has been designed with a demonstration on MobileNet-SSD network involving atrous kernels. The benchmarking result proves that our design achieves even slight speed-up for atrous convolution compared to conventional convolution, other than visible performance degradation for mainstream CPU and GPU.

articleTitle: A 12-Cell Battery Monitor IC with 2-Channel 16-bit ADCs and Isolated Bidirectional Data Interface
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 12-cell batter monitor IC is presented for the battery management system of electric vehicles. To achieve fast and precise measurement, two 16-bit $\Delta-\Sigma$ ADCs are used in parallel for all the 12 battery cells, which are divided into 2 groups controlled by 2 separate high-voltage multiplexers. Two transformer-based data interfaces are designed to enable isolated bidirectional data transmission to a low-voltage MCU. Fabricated in a $0.18-\mu \mathrm{m}$ BCD process, measurement results with a 3.3-MHz on-chip clock show that all the 12 battery cell voltages can be measured in 1 ms with error less than 1 mV. The chip consumes 20.5 mA when it is in operation.

articleTitle: 6G Technologies - Opportunities and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The key drivers of 6G mainly result from the technology-driven paradigm shift. As a novel paradigm, interference exploitation will be used to design the energy-efficient and high-precision communication systems. The most potential interference exploitation is computational holographic radio technology. As one of the most promising 6G physical layer technologies, holographic radio creates an opportunity of converging RF holography, integrated photonics, optical computing and photonic AI. Although holographic radio largely improves spectral efficiency and network capacity, and promotes the integration of imaging, sensing and wireless communication, how to realize it is a great challenge.

articleTitle: A 77-GHz 1.5-mW Down-Conversion Mixer Using Active Loads Technique in 40-nm CMOS for Automotive Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A modified Gilbert down-conversion mixer for 77-GHz automotive radar application is presented in this paper. By replacing the resistive loads with active loads composed of resistors and PMOSs, the output DC voltage becomes stabler, and the suppression of even-order components is improved. Fabricated in 40-nm CMOS technology, the proposed mixer occupies a core chip area of 0.25 × 0.26 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The DC power consumption is only 1.5 mW with a 1-V supply. The measured maximum voltage conversion gain is 4.8 dB at LO frequency of 78.5 GHz and IF frequency of 20 MHz. The input 1-dB compression point is 0.8 dBm. Measured results also show that the reflection coefficient of the RF port is less than -11 dB from 74 to 83 GHz.

articleTitle: Low-temperature direct and indirect bonding using plasma activation for 3D integration
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this study, plasma activation is demonstrated as a surface activation method in SiCOI (SiC-on-insulator) substrate fabrication, silicon-based wafer bonding, and pressure-less Ag nanopaste sintering for 3D integration. Oxygen inductive coupled plasma (ICP) shows high efficiency in organic removal and surface activation, which not only achieves a tight and reliable direct bonding but also serves for pressure-less sintering of Ag nanopaste by pre-decomposing the organic components. The oxygen plasma activation has exerted its multi-functional nature and excellent performance in both direct and indirect bonding methods. We believe that the plasma activation has sufficient potential as a versatile and efficient approach for heterogeneous integration and high-density packaging.

articleTitle: A Wideband LNA with Gm-Boosted and Noise Cancel Technique
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 0.1 to 5GHz wide-band common-gate (CG) low-noise amplifier (LNA) in 130nm CMOS technology. The capacitive cross-coupling topology boosts the equivalent transconductance of input CG transistor. The active differential pairs for bias path contribute to not only noise cancel of input CG and bias transistors, but also flexible input matching. Moreover, the circuit is inductorless, only occupying an area of 0.015mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The voltage gain ranges from 17.7 to 20.0dB. The minimum noise Figure is 3. 04dB, and IIP3 is -1.7dBm. The circuit consumes 4.4mW under a 1.2V single voltage supply.

articleTitle: Hardware Trojans detection based on BP neural network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper uses side channel analysis to detect hardware Trojan based on back propagation neural network. First, a power consumption collection platform is built to collect power waveforms, and the amplifier is utilized to amplify power consumption information to improve the detection accuracy. Then the small difference between the power waveforms is recognized by the back propagation neural network to achieve the purpose of detection. This method is validated on Advanced Encryption Standard circuit. Results show this method is able to identify the circuits with a Trojan occupied 0.19% of Advanced Encryption Standard circuit. And the detection accuracy rate can reach 100%.

articleTitle: A Fast Response Digital Low-Dropout Regulator Based on Enhanced Analog Assisted Loop
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The digital low-dropout (D-LDO) regulator can work effectively in low supply voltage. It is appropriate for the digital circuits due to great process scalability. However, D-LDOs suffer a poor transient response caused by the limited sampling clock and the logic delays. Therefore, the transient performance needs to be improved. One of the solutions is getting rid of the control scheme related to synchronous clock. This paper presents an enhanced analog assisted (E-AA) technique for D-LDOs to reduce the voltage spikes. The proposed technique adds a current buffer (CB) and a switch compensated resistor (SCR) into the conventional passive analog assisted loop. The CB is used to amplify the loop gain. The SCR is used to prevent a second droop of output voltage during recovery. The simulation results show that a maximum voltage undershoot is 16.4 mV with a 5 mA/3.8 ns load step and a total capacitor is only 52 pF. Thus, the resulting figure-of-merit (FoM) is 0.41 ps.

articleTitle: A 100-Gb/s PAM-4 CTLE in 28-nm CMOS with Coarse-Fine Gain Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 100-Gb/s continuous time linear equalizer (CTLE) for four-level pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM-4) in a 28-nm CMOS process is presented. The proposed CTLE provides peaking at Nyquist frequency, as well as peaking at mid-frequency for low-frequency channel-loss compensation. In addition, this design offers a coarse-fine tuning gain adjustment. The dc gain covers a wide range from -9dB to 12 dB with step size of less than 0.3 dB, and the peaking gain at Nyquist frequency can be adjusted from -3.4dB to 20 dB with a step size of less than 1.2 dB. The CTLE consumes 54-mW from a 0.9-V supply.

articleTitle: Design of a Wireless Compact Implantable Electrochemical Biosensor System for Health Monitoring Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this work, a wireless compact general-purpose electrochemical biosensor system was designed for continuous health index monitoring in implantable and/or wearable devices. Two different modes, the SCAN mode and the COLLECT mode, are applied in the proposed design. During the SCAN mode, the redox potential is optimized to improve the robustness of the COLLECT mode by enabling a relatively high amplitude of the output current design. The total weight is 4.5 gram including a 0.5Wh Li-battery, which can be applied to freely-moving small animal subjects for over 24-hour. The Experimental results shows a linearity of 0.9997, and a sensitivity of 2nA. Nitric oxide and Nitrite are used to demonstrate the concentration of the proposed system. In-vivo experiment was applied in the joint cavity of the New Zealand white rabbit.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of High Density 3D IPDs (Integrated Passive Devices) on Glass Substrate
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A number of test structures for capacitors and inductors were designed and manufactured on glass substrate. The fabrication process of IPDs forming with TGVs, Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> layers and multilevel metal layers on glass wafer is presented in this paper. Three-dimensional full-wave electromagnetic field simulation tools were used to analyze the electrical properties of the capacitors, inductors on glass substrate. In addition, the comparison of electrical properties of thin-film IPDs on silicon and on glass substrate is given.

articleTitle: A Fast and Efficient FPGA-based Level Set Hardware Accelerator for Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Level set algorithm has been widely used for image segmentation due to its high accuracy. In addition, compared to the deep learning-based image segmentation methods, the level set algorithm can be implemented without training data, which significantly reduce the labelling efforts. However, the normal level set algorithm is still developed using software, involving complex computation with a large number of pixels and iterations. Also, the software implementation induces long processing time and large power consumption. In this work, we propose a FPGA-based level set hardware accelerator for image segmentation. The proposed hardware accelerators contain four design components: task-level parallel processing, image splitting processing, fully-pipelined processing architecture, and time multiplexed gradient and divergence processing engine. Based on the experimental results, our proposed hardware accelerator achieves up to 10.7x acceleration compared to the level set algorithm executing on CPU, with only 2.2 W power consumption.

articleTitle: Reliability Design of a X-Band 2× 2 Tile-Type T/R Module under Thermal Shock and Random Vibration
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the further miniaturization of RF systems, its reliability has become one of the key factors. In this paper, the reliability of a X-band 2×2 tile-type module with ball grid array (BGA) and redistribution lines (RDL) process is discussed. The impact of thermal shock and random vibration on the module is analyzed by finite element analysis (FEA). And the Darveaux life prediction model and the Steinberg's three-interval method based on Gauss distribution and Miner's law are used to predict the life of the BGA. Finally, an improved design is proposed to enhance the reliability of the module.

articleTitle: CRC-Aided Belief Propagation Polar Decoding Scheme for NB-loT Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Polar codes have been considered as one of the forward error correction (FEC) in the control channel of 5G communication. However, due to their capacity-achieving performance and low complexity implementation, in this paper a CRC (cyclic redundancy check)-aided belief propagation (BP) polar decoding an algorithm known as BPC is proposed for the narrowband internet of things (NB-IoT) system. The analysis and simulation results demonstrate that our proposed BPC scheme improves block error rate (BLER) performance in the uplink NB-IoT compared with other polar decoding including the successive cancellation (SC), SC-List (SCL), and adopted LTE Turbo codes.

articleTitle: A 53.1-to-64.5 GHz In-Phase Coupled Quadrature Injection-Locked Oscillator with Transformer-Based I/Q-Phase Differential Injection Scheme
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A in-phase coupled quadrature injection-locked oscillator (QILO) with Transformer-based I/Q-phase differential injection scheme is proposed in this paper. The proposed transformer-based orthogonal injection scheme contributes to widen the locking range considerably. The in-phase coupling scheme improves both phase noise and IQ mismatch. Designed in a 65nm CMOS technology, post-layout simulation results indicate that the QILO achieves a total locking range from 53.1-to-64.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a fast capacitance sensing circuit for 16× 16 sized sensor array
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a CMOS circuit design of capacitance array sensing, including a capacitor to voltage conversion (CVC) circuit, 12-bit 8-channel column-level single-slope ADCs, and a scanning circuit. The integrated circuit is implemented based on 0.35μm process. A high-speed scanning circuit is designed. ADC conversion speed is also improved so the conversion cycle is decreased. CVC and ADC adopt pipeline working mode to improve the speed of the proposed sensing circuit, which consumes 330μs for the whole frame (all 256 pixels). Simulation results show the capacitance detection range is 1pF-5pF, and the accuracy can reach 1fF. ADC conversion time is 9.1μs at 450MHz clock frequency. The total power consumption of the 8-channel column-level single-slope ADCs is 32.81mW.

articleTitle: A TCAD-based Study of NDR Effect in NC-FinFET
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, the cause of inverse drain induced barrier lowering effect in negative capacitance field effect transistors (NCFETs) is discussed, and a capacitance model is given. Based on inverse DIBL effect, negative differential resistance phenomenon could occur, and these two effects are hard to be removed. Since higher on-off ratio and lower NDR cannot be achieved at the same condition, their relationship with device structure is also studied.

articleTitle: A Ka-Band CMOS Programmable Gain Amplifier with 15 dB Gain Tuning Range for Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A Ka-band 65 nm CMOS programmable gain amplifier (PGA) for phased array systems is presented in this paper. It is mainly composed of transformer-based input/output balun, seven parallel binary weighted digital programmable gain control units. Redundant control bit design, and off-chip FPGA are good for programmable testing, state selection and application. The PGA's 3dB bandwidth is 31-37GHz, which achieves a gain adjustment range of 15dB (-6.7~8.3dB), stepping by 0.5dB. At the same time, the RMS error of phase variation is less than 3.9 degrees in 31-37GHz. The power consumption of the presented PGA is 9mW and the core area of the chip is 170 μm 620 μm.

articleTitle: A 44-52 GHz Reflection-type Phase Shifter with 1.4° Phase Resolution in 28nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a 44-52 GHz passive reflection-type phase shifter with high phase resolution in 28nm CMOS process. The circuit consists of a hybrid coupler and two π-network loads. In the π-network loads, variable capacitance is realized by the capacitor array. Compared with the previously reported 6-bit phase shifter with 360° phase shift range, the proposed phase shifter achieves 1.4° phase shift accuracy. Although the proposed phase shift range is 96°, it can be extended to an 8-bit 360° phase shifter by cascading a coarse-tuning phase switcher. Across the full operating band, the post-layout simulated RMS phase error is 0.15° and the post-layout simulated RMS gain error is 0.34 dB, and the chip core area is 300 μm × 270 μm.

articleTitle: A Novel Variation-aware Error Monitoring Scheme for Memristor-based Material Implication Logic
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel error monitoring scheme for memristor-based Material Implication (IMP) logic. The novel monitoring method utilizes differences in the voltage of source-line (VsL) under different input cases after IMP operation, to detect two major types operation failures caused by gradual degradation phenomenon of memristor's positive threshold voltage (Vclοse). Simulation results under PVT variation show that the proposed error monitoring circuit in 0.18 μm technology can perform successful failure detection within two operation cycles, which can be used for periodic memristors failure detection and adaptively adjusting operation voltages during memristive IMP operation.

articleTitle: A Four-Channel Clocked-Analog Time-Division Multiplexed LDO with Shared Compensation Capacitor for Thermal-Optic Phase Tuning
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a four-channel clocked-analog time-division multiplexed (TDM) low-dropout regulator (LDO) that shares the controller between different channels. The controller includes an error amplifier with a shared compensation capacitor and a lightweight local generated supply that can support a wide supply range. Implemented in 130 nm CMOS process, the four-channel clocked-analog TDM LDO can simultaneously track four 50 kHz 1V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</sub> sinusoidal signals at 25 Ω loads and 5 MHz clock frequency with negligible crosstalk. The total chip area is only 0.056 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is 67.5% smaller than the conventional solution with four identical LDOs. This chip area reduction effect makes the TDM LDO a very promising choice in applications that require a large number of tunable supplies with small output power, e.g., thermal-optic phase shifters in silicon photonics.

articleTitle: A Simultaneous Wireless Power and Uplink Data Transfer System with Ultra-Low Crosstalk between the Power and Data Link
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Baes on the same inductive link, a pulse phase modulation method is proposed for uplink data transfer in a wireless power transfer system. It is proved that the crosstalk between the power and data link is small. The proposed system was simulated under 1MHz resonant frequency for power transfer. Simulation results show that the maximum data rate can be 62.25kbps that is half of carrier frequency, and the bit error rate is extremely low. In addition, there is ultra-low crosstalk between the power and data link.

Author Keywords: simultaneous wireless power and uplink data transfer

articleTitle: A Compact 37-40GHz CMOS Switch-Type Phase Shifter with Fine-Tuning Stage Achieving 0.4-dB RMS Gain Error
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an area-efficient 37-40 GHz CMOS switch-type phase shifter (STPS) for the 5th generation mobile network (5G). The proposed phase shifter is composed of four coarse phase shifting stages and a high-resolution tuning stage. The T-type STPS-based coarse stages realize a 22.5°-step phase shifting. To improve the phase shifting resolution with a simplified voltage control algorithm and a suppressed insertion loss, a compact tuning stage covering 23° is integrated in the phase shifter. Less than 1° resolution is realized for supporting the fine beam-steering and phase calibration in the future 5G new radio. In the measurement, the achieved RMS gain error at 39 GHz is 0.4 dB for the fine stage. The occupied core area for the proposed phase shifter including the fine-tuning stage is only 0.12mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in 65-nm CMOS.

articleTitle: Pseudo-NMOS Logic Circuits using ITO-Stabilized ZnO TFTs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, the 2-input/3-input XORs and majority gate based on ITO TFT are presented. The proposed circuits have a new pseudo-NMOS design style with a controllable pull-up device, whose advantages include a high noise margin and a high switching speed. At 5 V power supply, its measured results showed that the maximum delays of 2-inputs XOR, 3-input XOR and majority gate in this style are 5.20 μs, 6.65 μs, and 5.85 μs, respectively. This indicates that the general TFT logic can be implemented in such a style and it can also support the probability to realize the large digital logic circuits with moderate frequency based on ITO-stabilized ZnO TFT.

articleTitle: A 62μW CMOS Programmable Gain Amplifier with Reused Current and Resistor-Ladder Achieving 37.8dB Peak Gain and 1.5GHz GBW
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a low-power programmable gain amplifier (PGA) with reused current and resistor-ladder for zero-IF/low-IF short-range ISM-band receivers. The proposed techniques benefit the PGA from three aspects: 1) The inverter-based amplifier reuses the binary-weighted current to boost the gain-bandwidth (GBW). 2) The programmable R-2R resistor ladder is reused as the averaging resistor of the common-mode feedback loop to save the chip area. 3) The pseudo resistors can provide DC bias for the PGA unit without using extra DC power. As a result, the chip achieves a dB-linear gain range of 43.3 dB from -4 to 37.8 dB with a gain error of less than ±0.5 dB. Moreover, it consumes only 62 μW through a 1.2 V supply and exhibits a GBW of 1.5 GHz at the high-gain mode. The PGA occupies a 0.018 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> active area in 55-nm CMOS technology.

articleTitle: Highly Integrated and High Efficiency S-Band Quasi-MMIC Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a high integrated, compact and high efficiency S- band GaN quasi-MMIC power amplifier is developed. It uses two-stage amplification to achieve high gain. The driving and intermediate stage matching circuit is designed by GaAs monolithic circuit, and the output matching circuit is designed by ceramic material matching circuit. The operating conditions of the amplifier are -2.0V gate voltage, 48V drain voltage, 100* pulse width and 10% duty cycle. At 2.7-3.7GHz frequency, the saturated output power of the amplifier is more than 60W, the power added efficiency is more than 60%, and the gain is more than 26dB. The perfect combination of broadband high-power and high-performance output and miniaturization integration is realized.

articleTitle: A Full-duplex Transceiver with Integrated Active Quasi-circulator Achieving Self-interference RF Cancellation over Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: To improve the RF self-interference cancellation (SIC) of the full-duplex transceiver and extend the operating bandwidth, we propose an orthogonal-vector-synthesis (OVS)-based cancellation strategy, where an active quasi-circulator is integrated to shrink the system area and reduce the hardware overhead. The full-duplex transceiver is designed in a standard 180-nm CMOS process with layout size of 1.5mm × 1.75 mm including pads. A total SIC of more than 65 dB over wide bandwidth of 82 MHz is achieved. The noise Figure (NF) is only deteriorated by 1.5 dB.

articleTitle: A Calibration-Free Low Spur Multi-Phase Sampling PLL
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a low spur multi-phase sampling PLL. It employs a 4-phase sampling phase detection technique to effectively quadruple the sampling rate, while still achieving low spur at the presence of quadrature phase error without calibration. The design is implemented with TSMC 40-nm CMOS and verified with circuit simulation.

articleTitle: A 24-27GHz Phased Array Transceiver with 6bit Phase Shifter and 31.5dB Gain Control for 5G Communication in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 24-27 GHz phased array transceiver with 6bit phase shifter (PS) and 31.5dB gain control is presented for 5G communication. The transceiver consists of 6bit PS based on the passive vector modulation topology, and two digitally controlled variable gain amplifiers (VGA) with variable gain control range of 31.5dB and 0.5dB step. LNA and PA with embedded T/R switch are optimally co-designed to achieve excellent performance of the 5.2dß NF and 14.5dBm OP-1dB. The transceiver achieves 2°-3.6° RMS phase error, 0.2-0.4dB RMS gain error over 24-27GHz. The core area is only 1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the power consumption is 160mW/250mW in the RX/TX mode.

articleTitle: Design of Improved KY Converter with Low Power ZCD Circuit for Wide Load Current Application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, an improved KY converter with pulse width modulation (PWM) is proposed. The reverse current paths under discontinuous-conduction mode (DCM) are analyzed. To eliminate the reverse current exactly, a noval zero current detection (ZCD) method is proposed and demonstrated. The KY converter is fabricated by using 0.18 μm BCD process with active area of 3.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The off-chip components of an inductor of 4.7 μH, a load capacitor of 4.7 μF and two flying capacitors of 100 μF are employed. Simulated results show that the designed ZCD can work well in DCM of the proposed converter. The power conversion efficiency (PCE) can be maintained above 90% over wide load range from 100 mA to 2 A, and the PCE is enhanced by 16.3% compared with w/o ZCD at 25 mA load current.

articleTitle: L-Band 10-kW AlGaN/GaN HEMT with operating voltage of 100V
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 10-kW L-band GaN power high-electron mobility transistor (HEMT) has been reported in this paper. The developed 10-kW device was combined with four 150mm gate width AlGaN/GaN HEMT chips, and a balance configuration was used in the device design. When the drain bias condition is 100V, the pulse width is lOus and the period is 10ms, the output power is achieved amazing 10.87 kW at 1.3GHz, and its output power density over 18W/mm with a power gain of 18dB and a power added efficiency (PAE) of about 70%.

articleTitle: A 100mV Input Voltage, Multi-step Self-Startup Boost Converter Achieving 50X Voltage Step-up with Standard 0.18 μm CMOS Process for Energy Harvesting application
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, a multi-step self-startup boost converter is proposed for energy harvesting application. To decrease the minimum startup voltage, novel body-effect control method of MOSFETs is applied to self-startup circuit. Besides, dual-phase charge pump is adopted to reduce the output ripple. In addition, multi-step startup strategy is proposed to realize self-startup process of the boost converter. The boost converter is fabricated with standard 0. 18 μm CMOS process. The active area of the boost converter is nearly 3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which guarantees high power conversion efficiency (PCE) at as high as 2 A load current. Simulated results demonstrate that the boost converter can kick start with 400 mV input voltage, and the output voltage can be maintained up to 5 V with minimum of 100 mV input voltage, where 50X voltage step-up is achieved.

articleTitle: A Fully Differential Ultra-Compact and High Isolation Transformer-Based Wilkinson Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An ultra-compact transformer-based differential power divider with low insertion loss and high isolation is presented in this paper. To achieve the impedance transforming and power combining, two differential transformers are connected in parallel in the proposed Wilkinson power divider. Shunt capacitors are added between the output ports for matching and isolation enhancement. Designed in 40nm CMOS technology, the proposed power divider occupies a core chip area of $396 \mu \times 156\mu$. Post-layout simulation results show that the power divider achieves an insertion loss (S21) of 1.37dB, an input return loss (S11) of 14dB, an output return loss (S22) of 21dB and a port-to-port isolation of 32dB at 28.5GHz.

articleTitle: First Demonstration of Closed-Loop PWM Wavelength Locking of a Microring Resonator in a Monolithic Photonic-BiCMOS Platform
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Microring resonator (MRR) is a versatile photonic device that finds a wide range of applications in communication, computing, and sensing. However, it is susceptible to fabrication, thermal, and laser wavelength variations. This paper presents a PWM wavelength locker for a MRR. The wavelength locker and the MRR have been fabricated in a monolithic photonic BiCMOS platform. The effectiveness of this design is verified by extensive computer simulations. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first closed-loop PWM wavelength locker for MRRs reported in the literature.

articleTitle: Trends in Optoelectronic IC for Recent Optical Module and Photonics Integration
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This is an introductory article for IC researchers and engineers to understand the main issues in current optical module and photonics integration. We will start from the bandwidth demand drivers, an analysis of the obstacles impeding bandwidth scaling, and other main issues for electrical and optical systems; then we will talk about the trend of the core IC's evolution which causes higher single channel bit rate. The way to increase the bit rate is not only dependent on the physical bandwidth of the transmitting channel, but also the order of the modulation. PAM4 will be briefly discussed here, since it has been standardized for many applications. We will introduce the configuration of current 400G/800G optical module and the coming photonics integration (Co-Package Optics). From there, we will discuss the trends in optoelectronic IC for recent optical module and photonics integration.

articleTitle: Prediction algorithm for micro-loudspeaker diaphragm displacement based on PG-LSTM with 44% MSE reduction
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In this paper, the author proposes to use PG-LSTM (physics guided long short-term memory neural network) to model the circuit and mechanical structure of the micro-loudspeaker to improve the accuracy of the diaphragm displacement prediction. Compared with conventional physical model, the PG-LSTM model takes into account the influence of temperature on the loudspeaker system, and reduces the displacement prediction errors caused by system nonlinear factors when the input signal amplitude is large. The experimental results show that the mean-squared-error and maxim-absolute-error of the proposed model is reduced by 44% and 53% compared to the conventional physical model respectively.

articleTitle: An improved approach of synthesizing of Cu-Ag core-shell nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: With the development of high frequency and high power SIC devices, the requirement of high temperature connection materials between chip and substrate is becoming higher and higher. In recent years, the effects of the size of nanometer materials to achieve “low temperature bonding” research more and more. But the commonly used copper and silver are both disadvantages, easy oxidation of copper and silver high costs and electricity migration issues. So scholars began to study Cu-Ag core-shell nanoparticles, which has the advantages of copper and silver. But at present, the preparations of Cu-Ag core-shell nanoparticles are immature, there are some problems such as low yield, the uneven coating, process complex problems. In this study, a new method is applied in the fabrication of Cu-Ag core-shell nanoparticles. By adding L-histidine and ammonia water as a new complexing agent, the silver plating rate was controlled better than add ammonia alone. The as-prepared Cu-Ag nanoparticles show good coating quality, with core-shell structure and oxidation resistance. The new formulation provided in this study can be used to further rapidly prepare Cu-Ag coreshell nanoparticles for chip interconnection.

articleTitle: Design and Development for CIS-WLCSP Using Vertical TSV Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Wafer-level chip scale packaging (WLCSP) using TSV technology has widely used in CMOS image sensor (CIS) products in mass production. With more IO and high reliability requirements, the new CIS-WLCSP structure using vertical TSV was developed. However, the isolation layer deposited by low-temperature PECVD suffer crack failure in strict reliability test. To solve this problem, finite element simulation tool was used for evaluation and the simulation results were verified by design of experiment. Both results showed the new design with passivation layer introduced as stress buffer layer was an effective and reliable solution for CIS-WLCSP based on vertical TSV.

articleTitle: A 10MHz Buck Converter with Type-III Control and Transient Enhancement Transistor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a buck converter with Type-III compensation and a transient enhanced transistor (TET) for portable devices. A large power inductor value is desirable in DC-DC conversion for reducing the inductor current ripple, and consequently improving the efficiency. However, the main limitation of the load transient response is the large power consumed by the inductor. In this work, we place a TET in parallel with the main power inductor. The transient control circuit detects the load transient from the error amplifier output, and controls the TET to charge or discharge the output. The proposed buck converter, designed in 180-nm CMOS, operates at 10-MHz and reaches a simulated 95.2% peak efficiency over a load range of 0.1A to 1.5A, at 1.8V of output voltage. When compared with the conventional buck converter, the proposed architecture reduces the settling time from 9.3μs to 3.4μs and the undershoot voltage from 420mV to 214mV, during a load change from 0.1A to 1.35A. Besides, it decreases the settling time from 10.4μs to 3.1μs and the overshoot voltage from 350mV to 58 mV, during a load change from 1.35A to 0.1A.

articleTitle: High-Gain PFD/Charge Pump with Gain Proportional to Slew Rate of Up/Down Signals
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A high-gain low-noise phase-frequency detector/charge pump (PFD/CP) topology is proposed. When input phase error is small, as in the locked state, the charge pump achieves a high linear gain and works without being fully turned on. When input phase error is large, as in acquisition state, the CP gain drops to Icp/2π as with conventional tri-state charge pumps. In simulation the prototype high-gain charge pump demonstrates a gain of 10x higher than that of a conventional charge pump with an input range of +/-100pS. A charge-pump contributed in-band noise floor of -116dBc/Hz is achieved, which is 18dß lower than that of a conventional PFD/CP with the same bias current of 40uA, in a PLL with 4 GHz output frequency and 50 MHz reference frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Memristive Quantized Convolutional Neural Network Accelerator with Device Nonideality
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Memristive convolutional neural network accelerator has attracted intensive interest in reducing time and energy consumption. In this article, we analysis the viability of the quantization method using LeNet-5 model on MNIST dataset. Low bit-precision quantization is achieved with slight accuracy loss. The fabricated bilayer AlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> memristor with 3-bit states is used to emulate the synapse, and an accuracy of 97.93% is accomplished within the device nonideality. Furthermore, the device requirements of variation and reliability on inference application are evaluated and proposed.

articleTitle: An Ultra-low Power Relaxation Oscillator with Novel Ultra-low Leakage Switch and Temperature-compensated Resistor
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultra-low power relaxation oscillator with novel Ultra-Low Leakage Switch (ULLS) and temperature-compensated resistor (TCR). The ULLS decreases the leakage current over 90 dB, and the leakage variation against temperature can be also reduced about ×67. The TCR designed for the oscillator can reach a temperature coefficient of 0.08% ppm/°C. By utilizing resistive frequency locked structure with the proposed ULLS and well-designed TCR, the proposed oscillator achieves higher energy efficiency and better temperature performance than most existing oscillators in literature. It has an ultra-lower power of 87.6 nW (with an ultra-low leakage of 3 nW) when operating at 75.9 kI z and 1.2 V in 0.18-μm, and the simulated temperature sensitivity and supply voltage sensitivity are 23.9 ppm/°C and 0.41%/V, respectively.

articleTitle: An A.I.-Based Fuzzy Logic DC-DC Converter for USB Type-C Charging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The modernized USB Power delivery (PD)3.0 specification with Type-C interface has become the worldwide fast-charging standard for electronic devices, covering a wide range of use. These power supplies require not only high power delivery but also an intelligent control to monitor the charging processes simultaneously. So, the design of Type-C charger with Digital-Fuzzy PID-control DC-DC Converter is proposed, which gives the optimized performance in Type-C PD charging applications.

articleTitle: A Third-order Sigma-delta Frequency-to-digital Converter Based on Reset Counter and PLL
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A sigma-delta frequency-to-digital converter (FDC) based on a phase-locked loop (PLL) and a reset-counter is presented. The reset counter is inserted in the feedback path of a conventional PLL to quantize the phase and calculate the frequency. Simple analytical model shows that the quantization noise is third-order shaped at the output of this converter. Besides, compared to existing conversion techniques, this converter turns out to be the most power efficient approach, which is suitable for analog-to-digital conversion in low-power frequency modulated (FM) sensors.

articleTitle: A 0.65μW 70nV/rtHz capacitively-coupled chopper instrumentation amplifier for bio-potential sensing in 28-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A low-power low-noise capacitively-coupled chopper instrumentation amplifier (CCIA) using stacked transconductance amplifiers (OTAs) for bio-potential sensing is presented. It utilizes stacked OTAs as the first stage for noise and power efficiency optimization. A DC servo loop is added to eliminate the DC electrode offset, and pseudo-resistors are designed to realize high-pass filters with ultra-low cut-off frequency without using large capacitors. The CCIA was designed in a 28nm CMOS process, occupying a chip area of 0.15mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It consumes 0.65μA current under 1-V supply. Simulation results indicate that the input-referred noise is 70nV/rtHz and the noise efficiency factor is 2.7.

articleTitle: An Asynchronous Convolution Process Engine forVGG-16 Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: VGG-16 neural network is one of the most powerful artificial intelligence algorithms widely used in computer vision. There are many accelerators proposed for VGG-16 to obtain high energy efficiency but ignoring the existence of the power-hungry clock network. In this paper, we proposed an asynchronous convolution process engine for VGG-16 whose multiplication and accumulation (MAC) are clock-free asynchronous circuits. We also proposed a novel synchronous and asynchronous interface to solve the problem of setup time and hold time violations that easily occur when synchronous and asynchronous circuits are combined. The whole design was implemented in the 4Onm process. Experimental results show that compared with the synchronous version design, our asynchronous convolution process engine can achieve a 1.5x improvement in energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Characteristics Analysis of Ferroelectric Tunneling Junctions with Different Structures
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: We successfully fabricated three ferroelectric tunneling junction (FTJ) devices based on Hf<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (HZO) ferroelectric film with different structures. All three FTJ devices can achieve the memory window of an order of magnitude. The DC I-V characteristics and band diagrams of three FTJ devices are analyzed and compared, and metal-ferroelectric-insulator-metal (MFIM) FTJ with AI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> insulator layer achieved the largest memory window and the lowest power consumption. Finally, the difference in electrostatic characteristics of FTJ devices with different structures are explained by band diagram. These results may provide guidelines for future FTJ memory design.

articleTitle: A 0.7-V Clock-gating Cell with Power Gating Technology and 1.56-pA Sleep Power
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: In digital circuits, dynamic power consumption caused by clock switching occupies a large part of the total power consumption. Dynamic power consumption can be effectively reduced by using clock-gating technology. In this work, a clock-gating cell is proposed with sleeping mechanism under 0.7 V supply. Power gating is used to decrease the static power. The proposed cell can be used in circuit with frequency up to 1MHz typically. Compared to existing design, this work stands out for lower leakage current of 1.56 pA, which is suitable for circuits in low frequency where low power standard cell library is required.

articleTitle: A Practical ROI and Object Detection Method for Vision Robot
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: For visual robots, accurate recognition of objects and extraction of useful features are the basis for the next action. In order to exclude the influence of non-critical regions and improve the processing speed, this paper proposes a target detection method based on regions of interest (ROI). Firstly, the preprocessing steps such as filtering, color space conversion, and contour extraction are carried out for the acquired image frames. Then, the contour mask is used to obtain the irregular ROI. After that, color, shape, area and other information are adopted to identify the target and extract features such as angle and distance. This method achieves excellent performance on monocular robots.

articleTitle: 90-94GHz power amplifier based on planar space synthesis network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A 90-94GHz power amplifier was designed based on 0.1μm AlGaN/GaN HEMT process. The amplifier uses a planar space power synthesis network to study the output matching circuit of the final stage, By adding a compensation capacitor, the insertion loss of the amplifier is reduced and the synthesis efficiency of the synthesis network is improved. Experimental results supply operation demonstrate 30dBm of output power over 90-94GHz with 19% peak power added efficiency (PAE) and greater than 8dB power gain. The chip size is 3.4×1.4mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Design of 16TOPS Efficient GEMM Module in Deep Learning Accelerator
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: An efficient GEMM (general matrix multiplication) module is presented as a key computation unit in DLA (Deep Learning Accelerator). The core is located in a system which consists of a RISC-V processor for scalar operation and instruction distribution, and PE (Processing Engine) for vector operation and tensor operation. This paper focuses on the tensor operation module GEMM, which provides a highly-parallel processing capability through innovative data preprocessing and memory layout. To provide enough flexibility for various neural networks, the GEMM also supports multiple instructions dispatched from RISC-V processor. Meanwhile, hierarchical instruction queue ensures the scalability. The proposed design achieves 16 TOPS INT8 at 1GHz when implemented with TSMC 12nm technology.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Processing Element Based on Asynchronous Data-Driven Bit-Serial Multiplier for CNNs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Owing to the existence of power-hungry clock networks, synchronous CNN accelerators are hard to achieve further low power consumption. In this paper, we propose a novel clockless asynchronous CNN processing element, replacing clock networks with asynchronous handshake signals. And then we construct a CNN computation array based on our PE and implement it in standard ASIC design flow. In addition, compared with the synchronous version that works at 200MHz frequency, our design can realize about 5.70× power consumption saving and 5.59× power-efficiency improvement when working at 196.0MHz equivalent frequency.

articleTitle: A Compact On-chip Analog Memory Cell for Storing TOF Image Signal in CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper designed and realized a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sup>×3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</sup> CMOS analog memory for storing TOF image signal on chip. In order to achieve high-density integration, NMOS transistor with minimum size is employed to be the switch and the storage capacitor is realized with a 1.8V NMOS transistor. The prototype chip has been fabricated in a standard 0.18μm CMOS process. The size of the memory cell is 4μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sup>×4μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V</sup>. The measurement results show that the analog signal can be written into the memory in 20ns, and the leakage current causes the stored analog signal reducing with a speed value of 0.33mV/ms. This memory cell can be expanded to a larger array and integrated into sensor chip.

articleTitle: A 28GBaud High-Swing Linear Mach-Zehnder Modulators Driver for PAM-4 and Coherent Optical Communications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper introduces the design, analysis and simulation results of a driver for high-speed silicon photonic modulators. To achieve the high swing and high linearity simultaneously, several broadband circuit topology and techniques are employed, including the pre-emphasis circuit, variable gain amplifier and push-pull output stage. The driver is implemented in a 130nm BiCMOS process, achieving 22GHz bandwidth, 4V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">PP</sub> output swing, 900mW power consumption in the post-layout simulation.

articleTitle: A Method of Estimating FD Capacitance with Large Size Photodiode in High Speed Imaging (Invited Paper)
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This work proposes a simple method of calculating FD capacitance in 2-dimensional (2D) TCAD simulation that combines with pixel layout, simplifying the estimation of CIS FD design. Approximate per unit FD junction capacitance can be extracted by few TCAD simulations. This method has been verified using an image sensor chip with 10um-size pixel fabricated in 180nm CIS process. The testing results show that the error percentage of FD capacitance between test and calculation is approximately 5.90%.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Millimeter-Wave On-Chip Resonator Design in Silicon Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel electromagnetic (EM) structure used for miniaturized on-chip resonator design in silicon technology is presented in this paper. The structure is based on a hybrid-element approach that consists of both lumped- and distributed-elements. Using this approach for resonator design, the resonant frequency could be effectively controlled without affecting other design specifications. To prove the concept, the designed EM structure is fabricated in a standard 0.13-μm CMOS technology. Based on the measured data, a transmission zero located at approximately 47 GHz has been found. The physical dimension of the designed resonator is only 0.17 times 0.15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Modeling the Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensor with a Polymer Composite Dielectric Layer
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: F1exible pressure sensors are important in applications of flexible electronics. Although extensive efforts have been made to improve the performance of pressure sensors through materials fabrication or circuitry design, the effect of loading mode on the sensor response has rarely been discussed before. In this study, an appropriate constitutive relationship of the composite material that is used as the dielectric layer in capacitive pressure sensors was characterized via tensile tests, thereby ensuring the stresses in the film sensor under a pressure can be simulated accurately by the finite element analysis. The stresses under the pressure head, as a major factor to affect the capacitance variation, were further fitted by a polynomial equation in terms of the variation of the capacitance of the film sensor with a designed experiment for both measuring the capacitance and force. The equation supports an empirical model that reveals the capacitance of the film sensor can be estimated directly when the stress in the sensor is obtained. The model helps to develop a new pressure sensor applied in flexible devices.

articleTitle: A 16Gb/s Triple-Mode Driver in 0.18μm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A large swing 16Gb/s triple-mode driver in 0.18 $\mu$ m technology is presented. The driver can transform the working configuration according to the application requirements to drive the modulator (MOD), Transmitter Optical Subassembly (TOSA) and laser diode (LD), respectively, with corresponding operating current in each mode to reduce power consumption. The driver employs open drain topology to maximize the modulation swing, and shunt peaking inductors to increase the bandwidth. The driver is able to deliver a maximum modulation current of 67mA and 100mA when driving TOSA and LD, consuming 216mW. When driving MOD, it delivers 2Vpp maximum modulation voltage, consuming only 132mW. The bandwidth in all modes is sufficient for 16Gb/s signal operation.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Parallel FPGA Implementation of Harris Corner Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Harris corner detection is a common operation in the field of image processing, but suffering from computation complexity in embedded system. The current method of corner detection is to process one pixel in one clock cycle. With the improvement of image acquisition method in modern society, higher processing speed requirements have been proposed for the implementation of corner detection. This paper presents a new pixel-level parallelism FPGA implementation for Harris corner detection, which double the processing speed or more with almost no decreasing in accuracy. It is implemented on FPGA in the high-speed camera, and the experimental results show that the implementation is suitable for real-time applications.

articleTitle: AppSRAM: Incremental Retraining Method to Compensate for SRAM Failure in Voltage-Scaling Embedded CNN System
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) has been used widely in many fields. But to deploy CNN on an embedded system, we need to overcome the memory power problem: the memory power is too large a part of total power consumption. It is very significant to reduce the memory power in embedded CNN system. In this paper, a new method called AppSRAM is proposed to solve this problem. By lowering the supply voltage of static random access memory (SRAM), the memory is treated as approximate memory, and the power of memory can decrease a lot. However, deploy CNN on this approximate memory would cause non-unneglectable accuracy loss because of the SRAM failure caused by voltage scaling. AppSRAM can use incremental retraining method to compensate for this effect. And thanks to both deploy weight data and intermediate data on approximate memory, AppSRAM can further save more power. Experiments show that by performing AppSRAM on an embedded CNN system (running Cifar-10 network), the memory power can reduce to 48% of original memory power while the accuracy loss is only 0.8.

articleTitle: An Enhanced 128-bit Asynchronous Authentication and Data Encryption Circuits for loT Sensor Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Today, AES and PUF circuits used in the sensor circuit is still valuable to adversarial attacks. To enhance its security without incurring any hardware resource, we propose to intermix and reuse the PUF and AES, creating a brand new PUF design based on PUF+AES+PUF architecture. As compared to our previous PUF design, the proposed PUF+AES+PUF has shown improvement in FAR and FRR of 4.45%, and 11.31%, respectively. To further reduce the performance of AES, we have proposed an asynchronous AES architecture, which has improved the power efficiency from 1.47Gbps/W to 2.19Gbps/W.

articleTitle: Microfluidic bioparticle separation and detection system based on standing surface acoustic wave and lensless imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Separation and detection of biological particles or cells from samples by point-of-care (POC) systems are very important for biomedical and healthcare applications. The acoustophoresisbased microfluidic separation technique has the advantages of label-free, contactless, and good biocompatibility. However, most of the separation techniques are bulky, requiring additional equipment for analysis, not suitable for POC-based in-field realtime applications. Here we proposed a platform, which integrates an acoustophoresis-based separation device and a lensless imaging sensor into a compact standalone system. Stand Surface Acoustic Wave (SSAW) is utilized for label-free particle separation, while the lensless imaging system is for the seamless detection and particle counting using self-developed dualthreshold motion detection algorithms. The results showed that the integrated platform was capable to separate, distinguish, and count microbeads of different sizes. We believe that such a platform and the design methods offer a promising POC solution for label-free cell separation and detection in biomedical diagnostics applications.

articleTitle: A Nonlinearity-Calibration-Free Reconfigurable ADPLL for General Purpose Frequency Modulation
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents an all-digital PLL (ADPLL) based two-point modulator reconfigurable for wideband or narrowband FM with optimum performance. In either case, the proposed modulator does not perform background digital calibration to overcome the nonlinearity of key building blocks such as a TDC, a DTC, and a DCO, while requiring only initial calibration for process variation and frequency pre-tuning over different channels. For the narrowband FM, the proposed modulator works as a 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-point modulator where a high-pass modulation pass is performed with FIR-filtered 1b DCO modulation. In the case of the wideband FM, a nested ADPLL is designed to realize an absolute-gain DCO within the two-point modulator. To suppress quantization noise from a ΔΣ modulated divider, a high-frequency 4/5 divider is directly modulated. A 3b DTC between the 4/5 divider and an integer divider also works as an antialiasing filter for low in-band phase noise. Simulation results show that the proposed modulator can perform not only 1Mb/s GFSK modulation with the modulation index of 0.5 but also SSCG or FMCW modulation with very high modulation index, achieving good modulation linearity without nonlinearity calibration.

articleTitle: An improved QPZD Ids, GV model for 0.1μm AlGaN/GaN HEMTs Process
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper present an improved quasi-physical zone division (QPZD) Ids model for 0.1μm AlGaN/GaN HEMTs process. Compared to the original QPZD model based on 0.15μm AIGaN/GaN HEMTs process, the short channel effect of threshold voltage has been considered In addition, the critical electric field E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> is based on physical principles rather than empirical formula fitting. An analytic E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>(V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</sub>,T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ch</sub>) expression is presented for carrying out the model for circuit design. The presented Ids model can accurately fit DC and RF measurements for different size of devices.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of Double Gain Boosting Inductor Cascode Amplifier at Near-fmax Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: A novel design of double gain boosting inductor cascode amplifier at near-fmax frequencies is proposed. Based on the gain-plane approach, a study on the mechanism of gain boosting of the traditional cascode amplifier with gain boosting gate inductance is carried out. Z-embedding network, which is similar to the source degeneration inductor, is proposed to further improve the power gain. With the proposed circuit design method, a 180 GHz high gain single-stage cascode amplifier in 65 nm CMOS process is implemented. The results show a power gain of 7.7 dB in 180 GHz with 2V supply voltage, which is 6.7 dB higher than the traditional cascode amplifier.

articleTitle: W-band Amplifiers in 0.1 μm GaAs
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents two W-band amplifiers in 0.1 μm GaAs technology process, including a two-stage amplifier and a four-stage amplifier. For each amplifier, the optimal values of transistor size and biasing points are chosen to improve output power and gain at working band. Conjugate matching and power matching can be satisfied simultaneously while ensuring unconditional stability at all frequencies. Transmission line matching and λ /4 transmission line are used. Both amplifiers exhibit peak small-signal gain at 94 GHz. The 3 dB bandwidth of four-stage amplifier is up to 10 GHz with a peak gain of 17 dB.

articleTitle: Research and innovation in behavioral decision-making, image recognition, and action control of humanoid robot
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper talks about some research and innovation in behavioral decision-making, image recognition and action control of a humanoid robot. At first, we show our ideas on the humanoid robot’s behavioral decision-making which is mainly about the advantage of crossing the minefield. Then for image recognition, we introduce the image processing for kicking a ball and present the processing effect of each stage. At last, we show particularly our action control for setting up and explain the meaning of each frame of this action. In conclusion, our robot can quickly and stably pass most of the terrains and adapt to various environmental conditions.

articleTitle: A 224-Gb/s PAM4 High-Linearity, Energy-Efficiency Differential to Single-Ended Driver in 130-nm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a reconfigurable high-linearity, energy-efficiency 112-GBaud driver with 4-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM4) scheme in 130-nm BiCMOS. The proposed driver incorporates a continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE), a diode-connected emitter follower, a high-pass filter (HPF) and a push-pull amplifier.By tuning the emitter degenerated resistor of the CTLE, the driver can achieve variable gain from -0.6dB to 9.3dB. A wide bandwidth is realized by utilizing an emitter degenerated capacitor. The proposed driver can transfer 224-Gb/s PAM4 eye with an energy efficiency of 0.19-pJ/b from 2.5-V supply.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Mechanical Response of Wire Bonding in SiP under Thermal-mechanical-electrical Coupling Load
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: The heat dissipation of chips rise the risk for reliability of the system in package (SiP). Sequential coupling FEM simulation method was adopted to evaluate the reliability of SiP. The sub-model technology was used to analyze the thermo-mechanical response of gold wire leads in the whole SiP device. Based on the simulation, the stress and temperature distribution of the lead wires are obtained. The maximum value is compared with the ultimate strength to evaluate the reliability of the product under working conditions.

articleTitle: A 41μA Direct Frequency Modulation IC for Indoor Voice Broadcast in LF Band with Background Frequency Calibration
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper presents a low power direct frequency modulation IC in LF Band for the indoor voice broadcast application. The IC is mainly composed of a current starved voltage controlled ring oscillator modulated by the voice signal directly. A digital background frequency calibration loop is proposed to calibrate the frequency error/drift. Fabricated in 180nm CMOS, the chip occupies an area of 2.52mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Under 1.8V supply voltage, the frequency modulation IC consume less than 41μA with a 5pF load capacitor. The measured conversion gain in the voice band is not less than 4.0kHz/mV.

articleTitle: Fully-Differential 100-Gb/s PAM4 Cross-Coupled Regulated Transimpedance Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: This paper describes a broadband differential regulated cascode (RGC) transimpedance amplifier (TIA) designed in 130-nm SiGe process. Cross-coupled structure and two common emitter (CE) stages feedback loop are employed to reduce input impedance. The simulation results show that the proposed TIA has 46.35-dB Ω differential transimpedance gain and 35.6-GHz bandwidth (BW). Overall, it achieves a clear 100-Gb/s PAM4 eye diagram. The total power consumption is 84mW.

articleTitle: Design of basic block of neural signal detection chip
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation, an emerging technology for the treatment of many neurological diseases, is considered an alternative to medical treatment and surgical treatment. This paper introduces the circuit implementation of the SVM (Support Vector Machine) module in the neural signal monitoring chip classifier. The support vector machine module includes an exponential function operation unit and a scaling unit. The exponential function operation circuit is designed based on the coordinate rotation digital calculation method (CORDIC). In order to reduce the amount of computation, some of unimportant or redundant features are removed from the complete feature set by selecting the patient's EEG (electroencephalogram) signal path. In addition, the decision function is transformed to optimize the transmission path of the data. Finally, the indicators for evaluating this system are given by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Design of Approximate Complex Constant Multiplier for Fast Fourier Transform in 28nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Mel Frequency Cepstrum Coefficients (MFCC) has been widely applied in voice interaction for feature extraction, where Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) takes up massive power consumption and area in the hardware. In the low-power serial FFT circuit, complex multiplication is used between process data and twiddle factors. To reduce the hardware cost of the complex multiplication, an approximate complex constant multiplier (ACCM) is proposed to replace the twiddle factor multiplication (TFM) module of the original FFT, which utilizes symmetry mapping relation of twiddle factor to decrease the number of constants of twiddle factor (TF). Meanwhile, approximate processing algorithm is used to increase the common part between fixed constants. Applied on a 128-point 16bit serial FFT in TSMC 28nm CMOS, our method reduces the area of TFM module by 27.4% according to the DC synthesis result at TT 25°C. It has no influence on the MFCC output feature, thus providing an effective and low-overhead method to optimize FFT/MFCC.

articleTitle: Design for Enhancing the Performance of Memristive Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 IEEE International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Technologies and Applications (ICTA)
abstract: Memristive convolution neural network (MCNN) has been fierily investigated. Commonly, linearly and symmetrically analogue conductance tuning behavior with low device variation is the basic requirement for memristors. Further, in this paper, one-transistor-one-resistor memristors (1T1R memristors) based LeNet-5 convolutional neural network is built for several important issues, including design of memristive weight cores, pulse update method, activation function and conductance dynamic range, even the overlapping of adjacent states. Incorporating all simulated results, some strategies have been proposed for improving the performance of memristive convolutional neural network and provide more alternative strategies for hardware neuromorphic systems.
